title: Blanket stitch
subtitle: A looped edge stitch that also works as an open line filler
excerpt: Blanket stitch locks a loop of thread against the fabric edge or along a drawn line with each stitch, building a row of upright bars connected by a continuous looped base.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), buttonhole and blanket stitch entries.
heroPrompt: Blanket stitch along the edge of a felt piece, evenly spaced bars with a clean looped base, cream thread on dark felt, close-up, natural light.

content.text: Blanket stitch and buttonhole stitch use the same motion. Blanket stitch leaves a gap between bars; buttonhole stitch packs them close together. Both work by inserting the needle from the edge or outer line inward, and passing the thread under the needle tip before pulling through so a loop locks at the base.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 3 strands for a bold edge, 2 for a fine line

items.label: Hoop
items.value: 15 cm hoop, or work in hand on stiff felt

content.text: Anchor the thread at the start of the edge. Bring the needle up from the back through the fabric, one bar-height above the edge.
Insert the needle straight down at the edge, one bar-width to the right. Bring it back up the same distance from the edge, keeping the thread looped under the needle tip.
Pull through. The loop closes at the edge. Repeat along the edge, keeping bar height and spacing consistent.

items.symptom: The base loop twists rather than lying flat
items.cause: Thread is not passing under the needle cleanly before the pull.
items.fix: Check the thread is completely under the needle before every pull.

items.cause: The needle is inserted at different depths.
items.fix: Mark a guide line one bar-height from the edge with a water-soluble pen.

content.text: Blanket stitch finishes the edges of applique and felt work. Packed tightly it becomes buttonhole stitch, used to edge needle-made lace and eyelets. In surface embroidery it forms decorative geometric borders and petal outlines.
